Subject: Dedicated pool — term lengths and start windows

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our infra and ML teams liked the throughput and KV-cache behavior of Redwood during the test runs. We're evaluating Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) for our inference layer and need to lock in a capacity start in early Q4.

A few things we need covered to move procurement forward:
- Pricing for 12 / 24 / 36 month reserved commits (per-GPU equivalent and monthly billing cadence)
- How you handle the ramp (we likely won't need 100% capacity day-one — options for staged activation and credits)
- Throughput guarantees (p99 latency targets at our target concurrency and token/sec profiles)
- Invoice timing and any onboarding credits for staging/beta usage
- Termination/early-exit levers (for procurement compliance)

Could you share a clean proposal we can hand to finance/procurement? We attached a short throughput spec for the cluster we intend to run.

Best,

Hi Ben — great to hear AtlasMed's team liked the run. Attaching a concise option matrix and an illustrative ramp schedule so procurement has something concrete. High level answers below; we'll follow up with pricing rows.

- Term options: 12 / 24 / 36 month reserved leases. Longer terms get stepped discounts and higher burst credits.
- Staged activation: we support a 3-tranche activation (10% -> 50% -> 100%) inside the first 90 days. Each tranche can be tied to an invoice milestone. Unused capacity in a tranche can be banked as credit toward future months in the first 6 months.
- Throughput SLA: we provide throughput guidance per GPU profile; for guaranteed p99 latency we offer a routed-lane SLA (regional low-latency lane) + soft burst pool. Specific guarantee depends on pinned model family and seq length — we will map against the AtlasMed spec you shared.
- Billing/credits: monthly invoicing is standard. We can pre-bill first 30 days on signing if required for internal validation. We typically offer onboarding credits (1–2 months equivalent) for 24/36 month commitments; 12-month leases get a smaller onboarding credit.
- Early-exit: standard termination fee applies (percentage of remaining commit). For regulated customers we can agree to a mid-term re-size option instead of immediate termination.

I've looped Karthik for pricing and Prioym for the exact GPU sizing/throughput mapping. Marcus and Monica are on the thread if you need contracting/terms liaison.

Attachments: Reserved_Schedule_v3.xlsx (proposed activation tranches and invoice milestones)

—Naomi

Ben, quick numbers to make procurement's life easier. These are illustrative — final pricing depends on final GPU SKU and model family. I'll put a formal spreadsheet into DocuSign/Drive once you confirm the preferred term.

Option A — 12 month
- Base effective spend: $85k / GPU-month
- Onboarding credit: 0.5 month
- Burst credits: 10% of monthly capacity
- Early-exit: remaining 40% of committed spend if terminated mid-term

Option B — 24 month
- Base effective spend: $73k / GPU-month (14% discount vs 12m)
- Onboarding credit: 1.25 months
- Burst credits: 20%
- Early-exit: remaining 30%

Option C — 36 month
- Base effective spend: $66k / GPU-month (22% discount vs 12m)
- Onboarding credit: 2 months
- Burst credits: 30% + one-time onboarding migration support credit
- Early-exit: remaining 20%

Ramp (proposal in Reserved_Schedule_v3.xlsx):
- T0 (signing): 10% capacity allocated; invoice month 1 for tranche 1
- Day 30: 50% allocation; invoice month 2 for tranche 2 (prorated for days active)
- Day 90: 100% allocation; regular monthly billing thereafter

If AtlasMed wants a later start date (e.g., Nov 1), we can set the lease effective date to Nov 1 but allow signing and pre-billing in Sep for procurement cycles.

Let me know which term you want us to flesh out and we'll produce a formal quote and redlines for the contract.

—Karthik

Ben — adding the SRE/SE perspective on sizing and guarantees. I reviewed the AtlasMed_Monthly_Throughput_Specs.pdf you sent. Key points:

- GPU sizing: based on your token/sec and concurrency profile I recommend a fleet composed of 60% A100-80GB equiv (for heavy chat/long context) + 40% L4-class for short, high-QPS routing. That gives better cost/throughput balance and predictable KV-cache behavior.
- Throughput guarantees: for the recommended mix we can guarantee median latency envelope and an SLA-backed p99 latency target for sustained bursts up to 75% of provisioned throughput. Anything above that goes to the soft burst pool (burst credits apply).
- Warm-up & KV priming: to hit p99 in the first week we recommend a 7–14 day warm-up window where AtlasMed seeds representative prompts (we can run replay). During warm-up, we accept that absolute p99 may be looser; SLA enforcement starts after the warm-up period.
- Staging band: propose a 10% staging bandwidth (free for first month for 24/36 mo) so you can validate models and operator runbooks without consuming committed capacity.
- Monitoring hooks: we'll provide token-level billing breakdown and per-route latency dashboards; SLO rule docs will be in the onboarding packet.

Happy to sync with your ML infra folks for one hour to walk the numbers and the flow.

—Prioym
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
